title: Form Validation
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of form validation and when it is appropriate.
Apply native html constraint validation using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check required fields and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study form validation and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Form Validation should guide users through a form rather than merely decorate controls. Associate labels and help text with fields, preserve native semantics, and validate submitted data on the server as well as in the browser.

content_blocks.alt_text: A flowchart sends form values through browser constraints, server validation, success feedback, or field-specific errors that return focus to the problem.
content_blocks.caption: Combine native constraints, server validation, field feedback, and safe re-entry.

content_blocks.title: Version and implementation note
content_blocks.text: Bootstrap documents limitations with its custom client-side validation styling/tooltips for assistive technology; include native constraints, clear field descriptions, and server-side validation.

content.task: Add form validation to a short form. Associate every field with help or error text as needed and test an invalid submission.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating form validation as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
